picked.t: Vietnam's $13B airport Long Thanh short of skilled workers two months before opening
picked.body: In a report sent to the government on Oct. 20, the ministry said several parts of the airport are behind schedule, with partial operations due to begin on Dec. 24. Airports Corporation of Vietnam (ACV) is the investor in component project 3, which covers the airport's essential facilities and is 86.03% complete by value of work done. Of its 12 construction packages under way, eight are expected to finish in December. The four at risk are the airport's internal roads and technical infrastructure, the passenger terminal, Cargo Terminal No. 1 and its auxiliary works, and the parking building. Work on the passenger terminal is 86.85% complete, with electrical and mechanical installation at 96.2%. Its structure is finished, but a large amount of work remains. Contractors there are struggling to bring in engineers, welders and specialized equipment installers, and slow paperwork has also affected payments and work on site. The terminal has 51 integrated load-test scenarios to check how its power, water supply and drainage, air conditioning, ventilation, firefighting and specialized equipment systems work together, but 16 have yet to be approved. Under the approved scenarios, the contractor has so far tested only the power supply, lighting and public address systems. The other systems have not been tested, and the investor has yet to set a date for finishing the tests. The internal roads and technical infrastructure package still has a large volume of work left but lacks enough construction workers, which the ministry called the main reason it cannot speed up. The remaining work also needs about 100,000 tons of asphalt concrete, but supply is severely short, making it hard to finish on schedule. At the airport's energy center, equipment has not been fully installed or test-run, either individually or together with other systems under load. Its readiness is a prerequisite for operating the passenger terminal, and the ministry said the target of completing it in November carries many risks. The ministry blamed the delays at all four packages on contractors not deploying as many workers and technical staff as they had committed to the investor. Slow paperwork has also left a large backlog of completed but unpaid work, and many packages have been paid little relative to the work done, affecting progress. The ministry called on ACV to push contractors to deploy enough workers, machinery, equipment, fuel and materials as committed. Where they fall short, ACV must determine who is responsible and act under the contracts to keep the project on schedule. ACV must also quickly resolve problems with payment for completed work and with changes to materials and equipment from the approved designs. Long Thanh, Vietnam's largest airport by area, covers about 5,000 ha in Dong Nai, some 40 km east of Ho Chi Minh City, and has a total investment of VND336.63 trillion (US$13 billion). Its first phase is designed to handle 25 million passengers and 1.2 million tons of cargo a year.

picked.t: Vietnam Airlines to launch direct Da Nang-Singapore flights on Nov 17
picked.body: The route will be operated by Airbus A321 aircraft, with flights departing Da Nang at 3:00 p.m. and Singapore at 7:45 p.m. (local time). The national flag carrier currently operates 14 round-trip flights per week between Hanoi and Singapore and 21 between Ho Chi Minh City and Singapore. Vietnam Airlines said Singapore is a key Southeast Asian source market for international visitors to Vietnam, with arrivals rising 29.8% year on year in the first nine months of 2026. Da Nang is among the destinations attracting Singaporean visitors. Round-trip economy-class tickets are priced from VND5.266 million (US$203.77), inclusive of taxes and fees, excluding peak periods. Tickets will be on sale until Dec. 31, 2026, for travel from Nov. 17, 2026, to May 31, 2027. In 2026, Vietnam Airlines has expanded its international network with routes to Amsterdam, Colombo and Phuket. It has also announced plans to launch Hanoi-Ahmedabad flights on Nov. 3 and Hanoi-Hangzhou flights on Nov. 22.

picked.t: A $8,500 night at presidential suite in Vietnam's tallest building
picked.body: A five-star hotel from the 47th floor up has 223 rooms and suites. The presidential suite takes up the entire 68th floor of the building. The hotel does not publicly list a tariff for the suite on its website, but a hotel representative said a one-night stay costs around VND220 million. Similar in size to a large villa, the presidential suite has separate areas for relaxation, guest reception, dining, and working. Its standout feature is its floor-to-ceiling glass wall that offers a 360-degree view of Ho Chi Minh City. From this vantage point, guests can take in views of the Saigon River, surrounding residential neighborhoods, and the city's road network. The living room has high ceilings, a leather sofa set, armchairs, and a coffee table, making it ideal for private and business meetings. According to the hotel representative, the living room's leather sofa set alone cost around VND1 billion. The presidential suite features a dedicated workspace equipped with a desk, chairs, and a balcony overlooking the city landscape. Adjacent to the living room are a bar, a dining room, and a pantry, complete with a separate service entrance for staff. This layout allows staff to prepare food and beverages and host catering events without having to enter the private living and relaxation areas. The private quarters consist of two bedrooms. The master bedroom is furnished with a king-sized bed and wall-to-wall carpeting. In addition to the master bedroom, the suite features a secondary bedroom, making it ideal for families or small groups. Both bedrooms are separated from the living and working areas, ensuring privacy when multiple guests share the space. The main bathroom is a highlight of the suite with a whirlpool massage tub positioned right next to glass windows. Clad in opulent marble, the space is fitted with double vanity sinks, a walk-in rain shower, and a standalone bathtub. Beyond its amenities, the guest experience is tailored through personalized services ranging from custom meals prepared by a private chef to dedicated assistance with meetings. Special requests may incur additional fees. The long banquet table area adjacent to the living room is configured to host private events. Guests booking the suite can hold private parties and events for up to 60 attendees. Overnight guests typically include business leaders, politicians, and celebrities who demand privacy and bespoke service. The clients who rent the space for events are usually high-end luxury brands. The living room, dining area, and bar can be customized and rearranged to match the event's specific theme. In 2026, the 68th-floor presidential suite was honored for the third time by the annual World Travel Awards, dubbed the "Oscars of the travel industry" as "Vietnam's Leading Hotel Suite" following earlier wins in 2023 and 2024. On online booking platforms, the hotel receives high ratings for its views, cleanliness, and culinary quality. However, some guests noted long elevator wait times and the hotel's location slightly removed from downtown HCMC, where major tourist attractions are concentrated. An aerial view of the 81-story Landmark 81 tower, the tallest building in Vietnam at 461 meters. At 488 square meters, the suite is larger than presidential suites at other luxury five-star hotels in the region such as the JW Marriott Hotel Hanoi (320 sq.m), Raffles Singapore (260 sq.m), and The St. Regis Kuala Lumpur (353 sq.m).
